title: Binary search: keep the half that can contain the answer
summary: Find 13 in a sorted list by comparing the middle value and narrowing the search interval. The ordering lets us safely discard half the remaining values.

steps.title: Start with a sorted list
steps.explanation: Our list is [2, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55]. We want 13. Binary search requires an ordered list so a comparison tells us which side could contain the target.
steps.takeaway: The sorted order is the reason we can discard a whole side.

nodes.label: Target: 13
nodes.detail: Search indices 0 through 6, including both ends.

steps.title: Check the middle value
steps.explanation: For seven values, the middle index is 3. Its value is 13, so this example succeeds immediately. A match ends the search.
steps.takeaway: Compare the target with the value at the middle index.

nodes.label: low = 0, high = 6
nodes.detail: The search interval covers the whole list.

nodes.label: Found 13
nodes.detail: Return index 3 because the middle value matches.

steps.title: If it is not a match, keep one half
steps.explanation: Now search for 21 instead. At index 3, 13 is smaller than 21: keep indices 4–6. Their middle is index 5, value 34; keep index 4. It contains 21.
steps.takeaway: Exclude the checked middle and the side that cannot hold the target.

steps.title: Stop when there is no interval left
steps.explanation: For a missing target such as 20, the bounds eventually cross: low becomes greater than high. Return 'not found'. Each comparison roughly halves the interval, giving logarithmic comparisons.
steps.takeaway: Binary search needs sorted data and uses O(log n) comparisons.

nodes.label: Middle matches target
nodes.detail: Return its index; a duplicate value may have other matching indices.

nodes.label: low > high
nodes.detail: No values remain; the target is absent.
